::: {.letter-metadata}
**Date:** March 25th [1893]  
**From:** Elderfield  Otterbourne  Winchester  
**Manuscript:** MS Princeton University, Parrish Collection
:::

My dear [Miss Wilcox](people/person_2120.qmd)[^1]
Fisher Unwin has sent me this letter asking me to forward it, and as you are the only person I know likely to be able to do so, I send it on to you, taking the opportunity at the same time of returning your book which has been most useful to me, I kept it so long because I found I had to lengthen out [Grisly Grisell](cmy_books/cmybook_228.qmd) and I wanted to refer to it

Yours sincerely
C M Yonge

---

[^1]: The recipient of this letter was evidently a member of the Wilcox family of Whitburn, cousins of Lewis Carroll, whom CMY had met through her friendship with the Collinson and Harrison families.  *Grisly Grisell* is set in Whitburn, and the book was probably a local history.  [Margaret Wilcox](people/person_1517.qmd) was dead, and this letter was perhaps addressed to her younger sister Isabella, who was still living in Whitburn at the time of the 1891 census.
